# Chairperson 

Email: [chair@alnwickdolphins.com](mailto:chair@alnwickdolphins.com)

The club chair is the principal officer for the club and is elected by the club 
members.

The chair provides direction and leadership to the club, dealing with issues as 
and when they arise. 
They are the 'face' of the committee and are intimately involved in all aspects
of club organisation.
This is a pivotal and highly rewarding role whose success and impact on the club 
will be determined by your own ambitions and enthusiasms. 
As well as your ability to guide and engage others, it is an opportunity to take 
on a new challenge and influence the future direction of your club.

Day to day jobs include but are not limited to:

- chairing meetings of the committee
- deciding the direction of the club
- setting the goals and vision of the club 
- ensuring the club meets its objectives and vision
- oversee decisions made by the management and other club personnel
- ensure the club operates within the relevant legal frameworks, including Swim England
laws

This varied role can (and does!) require a wide range of skills, including good 
knowledge of the club and competitive swimming, skills in 
organisation, diplomacy, public speaking and more.
The time committment is varied but can be considerable.
Its a challenging role but a massively reqarding one.

## Requirements

- Registration with Swim England
- DBS certificate
- Safeguarding training

[Swim England role profile](https://www.swimming.org/library/documents/126/download)

### Specifics

A more detailed list of tasks for the chairperson is as follows:

#### Every committee meeting

- Set/review the agenda with the Secretary
- Chair the meeting and keep discussion focused
- Check actions from the previous meeting have been completed
- Review any significant safeguarding/welfare matters with the Welfare Officer, while respecting confidentiality
- Review club finances with the Treasurer
- Review any significant risks or emerging issues
- Check for coaching/workforce issues requiring committee attention
- Review pool/facility issues
- Consider upcoming competitions, events and club activities
- Ensure decisions and actions have a clear owner
- Develop Committee Action Plan.
- Ensure minutes and key decisions are recorded

#### Regularly throughout the year

- Maintain a good working relationship with the Head Coach
- Check the club is operating in accordance with its constitution
- Ensure Swim England policies and requirements are being followed and sign off SwimMark
- Support the Welfare Officer and ensure safeguarding arrangements remain effective
- Ensure complaints/disputes follow the correct process rather than being dealt with informally by the Chair
- Monitor membership levels and club sustainability
- Monitor coaching and volunteer capacity
- Encourage recruitment of officials, volunteers and committee members
- Maintain good communication with swimmers and parents through regular Chairperson updates
- Send emails to parents for new starters and squad progressions
- Manage Swim Manager 
- Maintain relationships with pool operators and other key partners
- Keep the club's risk register under review
- Represent the club externally where appropriate

#### Financial oversight

You don't need to **do** the Treasurer's job, but should make sure there is appropriate oversight

- Review current financial position
- Understand major income and expenditure
- Monitor pool and coaching costs
- Check significant expenditure has appropriate approval
- Ensure membership/swimming fees remain appropriate
- Ensure annual accounts are prepared
- Consider longer-term financial sustainability
- Ensure appropriate financial controls are operating
- Signatory for the Bank Account

#### Safeguarding & compliance

Again, you're providing oversight, not replacing the Welfare Officer.

- Welfare Officer appointed and supported
- Appropriate safeguarding processes in place
- Required qualifications/checks for relevant roles are current
- Concerns are directed through the appropriate process
- Club policies are current and accessible
- Swim England affiliation requirements are completed
- Required risk assessments are maintained
- Chair/Welfare/other required training kept current

#### AGM / annually

- Agree AGM date
- Prepare Chair's annual report
- Review annual accounts with Treasurer
- Review committee positions and succession
- Identify vacancies before the AGM
- Review constitution and club policies
- Review membership fees
- Review club objectives for the coming season
- Review significant club risks
- Ensure Swim England affiliation/re-affiliation requirements are completed
- Confirm committee appointments following AGM
- Communicate priorities for the new season to members
